messages:
incident-bot: [P1] SLO alert: streaming gateway 5xx rate increased to 8% over baseline in us-east-1, spike starting 2026-03-14T17:22Z. Metrics: 502/504/CONN_RESET. Link: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/AL-1842
maria: ack. i'm oncall, looking now. creating #incident-1842-streaming
sanjay: grabbing logs from gateway. seeing a bunch of `chunked encoding error` entries and upstream 502 from model-vm pool
elaine: any customer reports? cs/ops pinged? 
support-anna: we have 3 customers reporting aborted streams and partial outputs (conversation cut at ~30 tokens). Severity Tier: customer A (enterprise) impacted intermittently
maria: initial hypothesis: gateway streaming path is tripping on certain long-lived connections -> backend VM returning 502 then gateway closes chunked stream. start live mitigation: enable fallback to non-streaming (buffered) for 20% of traffic while we debug.
jyoti: how do we flip fallback? Is there a runtime flag in the gateway or do we toggle at routing?
ken: gateway has header-based feature flag. set `x-redwood-streaming=disabled` on a fraction of requests via traffic-split policy. I can push a 20% rule now.
maria: do that, ken. also increase gateway upstream timeout to 60s (was 30s) as temporary.
ken: queued change — deploying canary in us-east-1 now. command:
```
# deploy traffic-split rule
rdctl gateway-rules apply --env=prod --region=us-east-1 --rule=streaming_disable:20%
rdctl gateway-config set --region=us-east-1 upstream_timeout=60s
```
maria: thanks. Sanjay, collect a tcpdump for one of the failed connections and paste the short logs here.
sanjay: attaching trimmed gateway log snippets (masked customer IDs):
```
[2026-03-14T17:23:11Z] conn_id=0x34ab chunked_write failed: write: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-14T17:23:11Z] upstream=10.2.4.8:8080 returned 502 Bad Gateway
[2026-03-14T17:23:12Z] request_id=xyz streaming aborted, client cancelled
```
elaine: seeing pattern: client cancellations + upstream 502s occurring within same 1s window. Could be VM OOM or fast transient networking flaps.
jyoti: checking model-vm side: control plane reports 502s coinciding with GC spikes on python runtime around those times. logs:
```
WARN process_handler: request timeout while GC paused
ERROR uvicorn: exception 'ConnectionResetError'
```
maria: actionable checklist:
- ken: roll traffic-split to 20% buffered (done?)
- ken: increase timeout (done?)
- sanjay: capture tcpdump on gateway and model-vm pairs for 15m
- jyoti: check VM OOM/GC, patch runtime to reduce GC pause (wip)
- elaine: notify CS for customers impacted and post temporary mitigation steps
ken: rollout completed. streaming disabled for 20% of new connections in us-east-1. gateway upstream_timeout=60s set.
maria: observing immediate drop in 5xx rate from 8% -> 3.2% (first 5m). good sign.
support-anna: informing customers: "We are experiencing intermittent truncated streaming responses for a subset of requests. We're routing affected traffic to a buffered path to reduce errors. We're actively investigating and will update every 30m." 
jyoti: we reproduced locally by sending high-concurrency streams with large context; model runtime GC pauses cause sudden close of connections. Two mitigation paths: tune GC / pause budgets; or make streaming more resilient (retry chunks, keepalive, detect and resend partial). Best short-term is to patch runtime to reduce GC allocations and schedule incremental GC.
sanjay: I've uploaded tcpdump and pcap to the incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/1842/pcap.tar.gz
elaine: can we enable SDK-level client retry for streaming chunk ACK failures? we risk reordering tokens for some clients.
maria: avoid client retries for live streaming; instead use server-side buffered fallback until runtime is patched. Next step: increase fallback to 40% if 5xx doesn't drop more.
ops-bot: automated note: created incident ticket INC-1842, linked runbook: https://wiki.redwood/infra/streaming-disconnects-runbook
ken: rolling to 40% now as a precaution.
maria: rolled. monitoring shows further drop to 1.1% over 10m window. keeping at 40% while we deploy runtime patch.
jyoti: pushing runtime patch to reduce GC pause durations (non-breaking). will deploy to canary group in us-east-1 model-vm pool.
jyoti: patch deployed to canary pool. telemetry shows 60% reduction in GC pause spikes. 
maria: great. plan: if patch stabilizes canary for 30m, we'll gradually remove buffered fallback and restore full streaming. otherwise plan B: longer-term runtime GC tuning + connection-level chunk-resume protocol (proposal in eng-runtime backlog).
elaine: I'll coordinate customer updates. CS will offer timeline and workaround (use non-streaming endpoint for critical runs).
support-anna: customers notified, one asked for incident RCA and timeline. logging that for postmortem.
maria: handing off to night oncall @sanjay at 18:00UTC. I'll keep monitoring and we'll reconvene in the morning for RCA. Thanks all.
sanjay: taking handoff. summary: temporary buffered fallback at 40% in us-east-1, upstream timeout increased, runtime patch on canary showing improvement, customers notified. will escalate if 5xx >2%.
incident-bot: incident INC-1842 updated: status=Mitigated, severity=P2 -> monitoring for 4h, postmortem scheduled: https://cal.com/redwood/postmortem-1842
